China is planning to construct 120 of them for its own use, at a cost of $13.2 Billion, or $110 Million apiece. Part of the money is to be financed by a small ‘Modernization Levy” that will be applied during the 2018 year to middle-income and above individuals. Although tax increases are not well received by the Chinese people, the support regarding this affair is much higher, likely due to exploding anti-Russian sentiment in the population. With China’s economy having grown massively over the last few years, being able to pay for this expense is not in much question… and with the recent deals with the Dutch there is little sign of it slowing down now.

China wishes to modernize its forces, and the Chengdu J-20 is a massive step in that direction. It is noted that it is:

“…the culmination of the latest in Chinese supercruise capabilities, airframe maneuverability, STOL (Short Take-Off and Landing) qualities and stealth technology. Stealth design philosophies of the J-20 revolve around much of what makes the American F-22 Raptor stand out in a crowd. Conscious attempts have been made to ensure that the new Chinese aircraft can compete successfully with the best that the major superpowers have to offer including use of strategic angles to deflect radar emissions, radar absorbing materials to retard the aircraft’s radar signature and an internal weapons bay to promote a less faceted radar target. The J-20 is believed to be on par with the American F-22 and F-35 fighters and the upcoming Russion Sukhoi T-50/PAK FA currently in development – joining an elite group of modern fighters to say the least.”
